memory_update.text: Energy Layer 1C should frame the opportunity as power availability and reliability across grid, data-center load growth, electrification, nuclear fuel cycle and generation reliability, not as a single commodity call.

Transmission hardware remains the highest-priority underfollowed node; PLPC currently has the cleanest public-market fit among supplied candidates, with Hubbell and Quanta serving as reference checks.

Dry-type transformers, power-quality products and specialty magnetics deserve a dedicated validation pass, with Hammond Power Solutions as the leading underfollowed candidate from the supplied context.

HVDC reactors and high-voltage grid-stability equipment are promising international discovery lanes; Quality Power Electrical Equipments should be verified for listing, liquidity, orders, customer qualifications and capacity.
Nuclear research should separate uranium mining from conversion, enrichment/HALEU and advanced fuel fabrication; some of the tightest bottlenecks may be private or buried inside mega-caps.

Second-order grid suppliers such as utility structures, galvanizing/coatings, inspection, robotic installation and field-labor productivity may reveal underfollowed beneficiaries if lead times become schedule-critical.

The current merged universe is grid/nuclear-heavy and still needs oil/gas reliability, LNG, pipeline compression, testing/inspection, protection relays, meters, utility software and grid cybersecurity expansion.
Before Layer 2 scoring, validate market cap, liquidity, current filings, backlog, capacity, customer concentration, margin expansion and valuation crowding for all candidates.

summary: Layer 1C merged the available Layer 1A theme map and Layer 1B node-level outputs into a balanced initial Energy universe. The strongest Serenity framing is power availability and reliability rather than a commodity-only call. Highest-priority nodes are transmission hardware, utility structures, dry-type transformers and power-quality equipment, HVDC reactors and grid-stability components, electrical construction demand proxies, corrosion/coatings for grid steel, and nuclear fuel-cycle bottlenecks. The universe deliberately keeps reference leaders for pricing and demand validation, but ranks underfollowed or niche public suppliers ahead of obvious mega-cap beneficiaries where evidence points to cleaner chokepoint exposure. Several candidates remain hypothesis-level because the supplied evidence includes external search context but not yet primary filings or current market-cap validation.
